subject: Deployment controls & isolation: Dedicated vs Private VPC — follow-up and proposed next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@acme-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Deployment controls & isolation: Dedicated vs Private VPC — follow-up and proposed next steps

Hi Alice — thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed set of next steps so your security and infra teams can validate configuration options.

Summary of customer needs (from today's call):
- Strict network segmentation and no co-mingling of production models with other tenants
- Customer-managed key material (KMS/HSM) and zero-access encryption for model artifacts and logs
- Audit logs for all inference requests with 12+ month retention and searchable traces
- Ability to host inference within a customer VPC (private control plane) OR fully isolated Dedicated pool with strict egress controls

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem): control plane deployed into your VPC, KMS integration, private peering, and optional on-prem package for air-gapped ops
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in our environment with strict network ACLs, per-customer tenants, and token-level audit logs exported to your SIEM via secure delivery

Questions for your security/infra team to confirm preference:
1) Does Acme require the control plane to be inside your VPC (i.e., no external control plane traffic)?
2) Is customer-managed KMS mandatory for all encryption-at-rest, including model artifacts and KV cache?
3) Any regulatory constraints that force on-prem only (e.g., explicit prohibition on cloud-hosted processing in our regions)?
4) Required RTO/RPO for inference availability (helps us size Dedicated capacity + SLA tier)

Proposed next steps:
- Tech deep-dive (90 min): our infra and security engineers + your infra/security to walk through control plane topology, KMS flows, and network diagrams
- Deliver artifacts: architecture diagram + VPC integration checklist (attached) and a one-page KMS integration note
- Draft MSA addendum for privacy/controls to share with procurement (if you prefer Dedicated or Private)

Attachments: [redwood-dedicated-architecture.pdf (diagram, 2 pages), vpc-integration-checklist.xlsx (checklist)]

Can you confirm the right attendees for the deep-dive and a couple of windows that work for your team next week?

Thanks,
Priyom
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Martin <alice.martin@acme-health.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Deployment controls & isolation: Dedicated vs Private VPC — follow-up and proposed next steps

Hi Priyom — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Helpful. A few clarifications from Acme's side:

- Control plane: we prefer the control plane to be inside our VPC if possible. Reason: network-level audit trails and to minimize external egress for metadata calls. Is that supported for non-on-prem customers?
- KMS: customer-managed keys are required for all PHI-related data. Do you support HSM-backed keys (we use AWS KMS with custom key store / CloudHSM)?
- Audit logs: 24 months preferred, searchable and delivered to our Splunk instance over HTTPS/S3.
- Procurement: looping in procurement@acme-health.com to start the contracting timeline. They will need a high-level SOW and a draft of the security addendum.

People for the deep-dive:
- Myself (Alice Martin, Head of Security)
- Jared Lee (Network Lead) — will join if the control plane/VPC discussion is deep
- Procurement (copied) will sit in for scope/timeline items

Tentative availability: Tue 12/1 between 10–12 PT or Wed 12/2 after 1pm PT.

Thanks,
Alice
Chief Information Security Officer
Acme Health
